Apollo. One of the most complex and important Olympian deities in classical Greek and Roman mythology. He is the god of archery, music, dance, truth, prophecy, healing, diseases, poetry, and the sun. The twin brother of Artemis, Apollo was born on the island of Delos and is famously associated with his primary sanctuary at Delphi, home of the Pythian oracle.

He established the Oracle of Delphi after slaying the giant serpent Python, which was sent by Hera to persecute his pregnant mother Leto. He cursed the Trojan princess Cassandra with the burden of accurate prophecies that would never be believed, after she rejected his romantic advances. He was born along with his twin sister Artemis on the floating island of Delos, the only land that would grant asylum to their mother Leto. He flayed the satyr Marsyas alive after Marsyas challenged him to a musical contest and lost. He accidentally killed his male lover Hyacinthus with a stray discus, transforming his spilled blood into the hyacinth flower. He was pursuing the nymph Daphne when she prayed for escape and was transformed into a laurel tree, which subsequently became the god's sacred plant. As the son of Zeus and the brother of Athena, Apollo holds a central place in the Olympian pantheon and plays important roles in many major myths, including his connection to Cassandra and Laocoon during the events of the Trojan War.
